kernel_of_truth.description: The pre-1990 NMP drift IS qualitatively slow and roughly linear over century-scale windows — both PROS-002's framing (raw-text/02-wins.txt:21 'slow linear precession') and the NOAA NGDC gufm1+IGRF reconstructions agree on the qualitative shape (data/wins.json:WIN-006.detail_evidence ascribes 10–15 km/yr to pre-1990 drift). The dome correctly identified a real, well-documented phenomenon and bet on the pre-1990 trajectory being roughly linear — descriptively correct, which is non-trivial. The dome ALSO correctly committed to a specific numerical scale (0.0466 deg/yr over 1590-1990) rather than the vague qualitative claims many flat-Earth assertions trade in; that numerical specificity is itself unusual rigor for a dome WIN (data/wins.json:WIN-006.tldr_evidence).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Descriptive correctness about slope direction is necessary but not sufficient for confirmation under the dome's own predictive standard (raw-text/01-home.txt 'timestamped before confirming data was pulled,' echoed in data/wins.json:WIN-006.detail_verdict_text). Standard geophysics also describes the slope (data/wins.json:WIN-006.detail_evidence cites core-mantle convection / spherical harmonic models); the slope is non-discriminating. The specific numerical claim — 0.0466 deg/yr — does not survive reproducibility under any of three geometric conventions (5.17 / 1.00 / 5.17 km/yr against observed pre-1990 10–15 km/yr from NOAA historical records, data/wins.json:WIN-006.detail_evidence). And on the dome's own centuries-averaged 1590-1990 scale (raw-text/02-wins.txt:22), the gufm1+IGRF reconstruction gives ~1.82 km/yr (0.0164 deg/yr) — the dome's regression slope is ~2.84× too fast. The dome wins the qualitative description and the numerical specificity; it loses the actual numerical match on every scale we can test (data/wins.json:WIN-006.tldr_verdict, monitor/curmudgeon/reviews/WIN-006.c6.json quantitative_verification block reproducing this cycle).

Your observed-rate comparison cites 10-15 km/yr from NOAA historical records — that is a recent-decades rate, not the centuries-averaged rate the dome's number is indexed against. quantitative_verification.computations: (1) 0.0466 deg/yr × 111 km/deg = 5.17 km/yr great-circle. ✓ matches detail_verdict_text. (2) At NMP-1990 latitude 78.9°N, longitude-only rate = 5.17 × cos(78.9°) = 5.17 × 0.1925 = 0.996 km/yr. ✓ matches detail_verdict_text 1.0 km/yr (lower end of the 1.0–5.2 km/yr range). (3) gufm1 endpoints (74°N 273°E in 1590; 78.9°N 254°E in 1990): spherical law of cosines d = R × arccos(sin lat1 sin lat2 + cos lat1 cos lat2 cos Δlon) with R=6371 km, Δlon=19°: sin(74°)sin(78.9°) + cos(74°)cos(78.9°)cos(19°) = 0.9430 + 0.0534×0.9455 = 0.9935; arccos(0.9935) = 6.55° = 0.1144 rad; d = 6371 × 0.1144 = 729.4 km. ✓ matches c6 quantitative_verification. (4) 729.4 km / 400 yr = 1.823 km/yr; ÷ 111 km/deg = 0.01640 deg/yr. Dome 0.0466 / observed 0.01640 = 2.84× too fast. ✓ matches c6 numbers exactly.
